subtopic: XLA / Static vs dynamic shape handling
learningObjective: Understand XLA's static-shape orientation and how dynamic shape is handled (bucketing, dynamic dims, StableHLO dynamic ops).
stem: Which statements about static vs dynamic shape handling in XLA / StableHLO are correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: StableHLO includes `dynamic_*` ops (e.g., `dynamic_reshape`, `dynamic_slice`, `real_dynamic_slice`) that let programs represent computations whose shapes depend on runtime values without requiring re-compilation for every value.
XLA achieves dynamic-shape support by removing all shape annotations from HLO; static shapes are only used for debug logging and are not required by any optimization pass.
Serving systems using XLA often mitigate re-compilation cost by shape bucketing / padding: routing many similar shapes to a small fixed set of pre-compiled shape configurations.

XLA is fundamentally static-shape-oriented: each HLO computation is specialized for concrete shapes at compile time, so shape changes typically trigger a fresh compilation (potentially very costly if unbounded).

explanation: Options A, C, D are correct; option B is incorrect. A (Correct): dynamic_* ops exist for genuine dynamic-shape programs. B (Wrong): static shape is preserved and drives many optimizations. C (Correct): bucketing is a real-world serving mitigation. D (Correct): XLA is static-first.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: dynamic_* ops exist for genuine dynamic-shape programs.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: static shape is preserved and drives many optimizations.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: bucketing is a real-world serving mitigation.

assumptions: XLA / StableHLO static-first orientation as documented.
nonImplications: Does not imply XLA cannot handle any dynamic shape.
Does not imply dynamic ops are always as fast as static ones.

distractorRationales.B: Wrong claim that static shape is discarded.
